subject: Next steps: model fit, safety probes & procurement checklist
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Morgan <lydia@acmemed.com>, Dr. Arun Patel <arun.patel@acmemed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery — model fit & safety priorities

Lydia / Arun — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of call:
- Primary goal: triage model options for Acme Med's triage-assistant flow (symptom intake + routing) with strict refusal/triage safety in sensitive cases (mental health, suicidal ideation, medication interactions).
- Success metrics you prioritized: refusal consistency (safety coverage), 98% uptime SLA for peak hours, 30% TCO reduction vs current hosted vendor.
- Data constraints: clinical notes will be de-identified in the pilot; production will require VPC + customer-managed keys (we discussed Redwood Private).

Redwood recommendations (initial):
- Candidate model family: Redwood-RT-13B (balanced latency/cost) for pilot eval; Redwood-XS-7B for cached/non-sensitive prompts; Redwood-CTX-70B for controlled high-quality fallbacks on complex cases.
- Safety approach: a two-layer strategy — (1) targeted refusal/safety probe evals + guardrail prompt sets, (2) policy layer with explicit classifier fallback for borderline cases.
- Benchmarks to run: hallucination precision (clinic QA set), refusal consistency (sensitive-domain suite), latency P95 on your median-turn lengths.

Attachments / artifacts I’m sending now:
- acme_med_prompt_set_v1.csv (seed prompts + guardrail probes) [Attachment: acme_med_prompt_set_v1.csv (text/csv)]
- benchmark_results_q1.pdf (example benchmark we ran against a similar workload) [Attachment: benchmark_results_q1.pdf (application/pdf)]
- Shared eval folder: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/acme-med-evals-2026

Open questions for you (so we can scope the eval):
1) For the pilot, can you confirm whether logs will be accessible to Redwood under a Data Processing Agreement? (helps with quality regression monitoring)
2) Do you need HIPAA BAAs in place before we start ingesting any de-identified clinical prompts into the eval harness?
3) What volume do you expect for the 2-week pilot (avg QPS / peak concurrency)?

Proposed next steps & owners:
- Rishi (@rishi_malhotra) will run an initial safety probe matrix against Redwood-RT-13B and Redwood-CTX-70B using the attached prompt set — target: deliver results by EOD Wed 2/18.
- Marissa will draft a mutual action plan and coordinate procurement contacts (DocuSign path) — cc’d.
- Ben and I will follow up on pricing scenarios (reserved vs hosted) after the eval readout.

If that sounds right I’ll kick off the eval and set a short weekly sync.

Thanks —

Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Discovery — model fit & safety priorities

Thanks, Jasmine — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) HIPAA / compliance: Our security team requires a signed BAA before any PHI (even de-identified clinical notes) are moved to a vendor environment. For the pilot we can provide a synthetic de-identification of 1k sample prompts if that helps you start the probe, but legal will need the BAA signed before we share anything closer to production data.

2) Refusal behavior: Two things matter most to us — (a) consistent refusal for instructions that could encourage self-harm or unsafe dosing, and (b) conservative stance on medication advice (we prefer explicit referral to clinicians). Can you confirm that your safety probes include few-shot and instruction-injection style prompts (we’ll attach examples after the BAA)?

3) Procurement: We’d like to see a simple two-phase pricing: short pilot pricing + optional committed capacity for the production rollout. Procurement added me on the cc; they are the decision owners for contracts.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the eval — can your team start the safety probes against synthetic prompts while legal reviews the BAA?

Best,

Lydia Morgan
Head of Product, Acme Medical
lydia@acmemed.com

Subject: Re: Discovery — model fit & safety priorities

Thanks — starting the run now against the synthetic prompt set. Quick notes on the eval plan I’m executing: 

- Models: Redwood-RT-13B (primary), Redwood-CTX-70B (fallback). Also including a lightweight baseline (Redwood-XS-7B) to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Probes: 1,200 synthetic safety probes (instruction-injection, disguised prompts, adversarial rewrite, few-shot escalation). We will tag each probe with the trigger type and expected refusal class.
- Metrics: refusal_consistency (binary per probe), refusal_precision (TP/(TP+FP)), hallucination_rate, latency_p95.
- Output artifacts: readout PDF, csv with per-probe responses, a suggested guardrail prompt list (three tiers: strict refuse, safe-redirect, escalate-to-human).

I’ll push results to the shared folder: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/acme-med-evals-2026/results and attach the safety probe scripts (stub) here.

[Attachment: safety_probe_scripts.zip (application/zip)]

ETA: EOD 2026-02-18 for the initial run; if we see high failure rates on refusal consistency we’ll propose an additional fine-tune or classifier-based fallback.
